content.thinking: Now drafting the postmortem, I want to flag that the ZeroDivisionError cause is inferred from log/flag correlation and confirmed by the revert, that the code fix PR is still a draft and unmerged (the flag is off, not the bug fixed), and that only one production change event was reviewed before attributing cause to the flag. I'll keep the executive summary free of component names, referring instead to "the online shop's account pages," and state the incident duration plainly as six minutes, from 15:32 to 15:38.

assumptions: The root cause was not reproduced or verified in code. It is inferred from three things lining up: the flag rollout timing, the ZeroDivisionError appearing in the logs in the same minute the flag went partially on, and the recovery after the flag was reverted.

Impact is assumed to be limited to account pages, because those were the only failing requests in the log window that was read. Only seven minutes of logs and one service's metrics were examined, so impact on downstream or dependent services was not checked.
The residual ~1% of errors present before and after the incident (ClientDisconnected, i.e. shoppers closing the connection) is assumed to be normal background noise and unrelated to this incident.

One production change (deploy/release) was found in the 67 minutes before the alert. It was not explicitly ruled out as a contributing factor; the flag was accepted as the cause once the revert worked. If that deploy is what shipped the spend-summary code, it is relevant context for the fix.

Recovery was judged from the service returning to its baseline error rate roughly 20 seconds after the revert. No check was made that the flag change had fully propagated to every instance, nor that any in-flight or partially rendered account pages were correct.

The specific data condition that makes the division zero (e.g. accounts with no spend in the period) was not identified; it is assumed to affect only a subset of accounts, since not all account requests failed while the flag was fully on.
The proposed fix in the draft pull request has not been validated; it is assumed to be unverified until reviewed and tested.
input.executive_summary: On 27 September 2026, for about six minutes in the mid-afternoon (15:32–15:38 UTC), a newly switched-on feature on the online shop caused the account page to fail for a large share of the shoppers who tried to open it. Those shoppers saw an error instead of their account page; retrying would not have helped while the feature was on. Other parts of the shop showed no errors in the logs reviewed. The automated on-call system picked up the alert, traced the failures to the feature that had just been turned on, switched it back off, and watched the page return to its normal behaviour before closing the incident out. The feature remains off. A draft code change to fix the underlying defect has been proposed but is not yet reviewed or merged, so the feature should stay off until it is.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was rolled out on io-shop (partially at 15:32, fully on by 15:33), and the newly enabled code path hit a ZeroDivisionError at `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47` when rendering the monthly spend summary on account pages, so every request that evaluated the flag on and took that path returned an error. Turning the flag back off removed the code path and the error rate returned to its prior level, which confirms the flag as the trigger; the underlying division-by-zero defect is still in the code.
